security_audit.summary: Most Ruby backtick findings are false positives from Markdown code fences and inline code in SKILL.md. The audit confirms package-installation and host-command examples, including two sudo commands, while reference URLs are documentation links only.

remediation.suggestion: Remove sudo commands from agent-facing workflows or require explicit user approval before any privileged package installation.
Label pip, brew, Python, and script commands as optional manual steps and avoid instructing agents to run them automatically.

remediation.issue: Referenced scripts and templates are not included in this package
remediation.suggestion: Either include the referenced files or state that they are examples so users do not run unexpected local scripts.

content.value_statement: Security teams need repeatable threat models that fit design and CI workflows. This skill guides pytm-based STRIDE modeling, DFD creation, and mitigation tracking.
actual_capabilities: Guides creation of pytm models with actors, boundaries, servers, datastores, and data flows.
Explains STRIDE review steps for threats, mitigations, residual risk, and acceptance criteria.
Provides example patterns for web applications, microservices, custom threats, trust boundaries, and risk scoring.
Shows how to generate reports and diagrams from pytm workflows.
Outlines CI integration patterns for threat model checks and artifact upload.
limitations: The skill contains documentation only; it does not include executable scripts or templates in this package.
Users must install pytm and Graphviz separately before generating diagrams.
Threat quality depends on accurate architecture details and security attributes.
It does not replace expert security review for high-risk systems.

use_cases.title: Model a New Web Application
use_cases.description: Create a pytm model with trust boundaries, components, sensitive data flows, and STRIDE review steps.

use_cases.title: Add Threat Modeling to CI
use_cases.description: Plan repeatable checks that generate reports, track mitigations, and publish diagram artifacts during builds.

use_cases.title: Review Architecture Changes
use_cases.description: Compare updated services, data stores, and trust boundaries against existing threats and mitigations.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Starter Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a pytm threat model for [system]. Ask for actors, components, trust boundaries, data flows, and sensitive data first.

prompt_templates.title: Review STRIDE Threats
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my pytm model for STRIDE coverage. Identify likely missing threats, mitigations, and residual risk questions.

prompt_templates.title: Add CI Checks
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a CI workflow for this pytm project. Include dependency setup, report generation, unmitigated threat checks, and artifact handling.

prompt_templates.title: Extend Risk Scoring
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me add custom threat definitions and risk scoring for [domain]. Map each threat to business impact and mitigation ownership.

output_examples.input: A product team needs a threat model for a three-tier web app.
output_examples.output: A structured model outline with actors, trust boundaries, data flows, sensitive data labels, and STRIDE review priorities.

output_examples.input: A CI pipeline should block unmitigated high-risk threats.
output_examples.output: A build plan that prepares prerequisites, runs the model, checks mitigation status, and publishes diagram and report artifacts.

output_examples.input: A team sees too many irrelevant threats in a report.
output_examples.output: A review checklist for component properties, trust boundaries, threat conditions, and documented non-applicable threats.

best_practices: Start with clear trust boundaries, data classifications, and authentication assumptions.
Keep threat models in version control and review changes with architecture updates.
Document mitigation ownership, residual risk, and approval criteria for each significant threat.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode real credentials, secrets, or private architecture details in shared models.
Do not treat generated threats as complete without human review.
Do not run installation or local script commands without user approval.

faq.question: What is pytm?
faq.answer: pytm is a Python library for defining architecture, data flows, and STRIDE threats as code.

faq.question: Does this skill generate diagrams directly?
faq.answer: It explains the workflow. Diagram generation requires pytm, Graphviz, and a local threat model file.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Does it include scripts or templates?
faq.answer: No. This package contains SKILL.md only; referenced scripts and templates are workflow examples.

faq.question: Is it safe for CI use?
faq.answer: Use it with reviewed dependencies, pinned versions, and approval for package installation steps.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide scope, components, trust boundaries, data flows, protocols, sensitive data, controls, and constraints.
